The Discourse on Psychic Power:
Is there the psychic power of intention belonging to either Buddhas or their disciples? Yes.
“May there be trees with evergreen leaves”—is this the supernormal power of intention (adhippāya-iddhi) belonging to Buddhas or their disciples?
One should not say so... [and so on].
“May the trees have perpetual flowers … may the trees have perpetual fruit … may there be perpetual light.”
“May there always be security… may there always be an abundance of food… may there always be well-being.”
Is there the power of resolve (adhippāya-iddhi) for Buddhas or for disciples?
One should not say so...
[as before] ... Is there the power of resolve for Buddhas or for disciples?
“Yes,” [he replies].
“Is there the supernormal power of resolve (adhippāya-iddhi) belonging to Buddhas or their disciples such that one might think, ‘Let contact that has arisen not cease’?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Feeling that has arisen … perception …” [and so on].
volition … consciousness … faith …
Energy … mindfulness … concentration … [and so forth] …
“May wisdom not cease”—
is this the supernormal power of intention (adhippāyiddhi) belonging to Buddhas or their disciples?
One should certainly not say so… [and so on].
Is there the psychic power of intention belonging to either Buddhas or their disciples?
Yes. [For example:
"May form become permanent."
There is the psychic power of intentionality … “feeling … perception …” [and so on].
“May volitional formations … consciousness be permanent”—
is there such an exercise of supernormal power through intention belonging to either the Buddhas or their disciples?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Is there the power of intention (adhippāya-iddhi) belonging to either Buddhas or disciples? Yes.
“There may be no beings subject to birth,” there is [this aspiration]...
“May beings subject to aging not grow old,” ...
“May beings subject to illness not fall ill,” ... [and so on].
“Is there a supernormal power of intention (adhippāya-iddhi) belonging to Buddhas or their disciples such that ‘may beings subject to death not die’?
One should certainly not say so… [and so on].
Is it not to be said that there exists the psychic power of intention belonging to either Buddhas or their disciples?
Yes, it is.
But did not the Venerable Pilindavaccha resolve that the palace of King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha was "golden," and was it indeed golden?
Yes, he did.

Since the Venerable Pilindavaccha resolved that the palace of King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha was "golden" and it was indeed golden, then surely it must be said: [that the mind can create what is not].
“There exists the supernormal power of intention belonging to either Buddhas or their disciples.
The Discussion on Supernormal Power is finished.
